summary: Rate-limit header misparse in SDK causing client-side retry spin and elevated 5xxs (customer: NovaHealth)
description: Issue summary: NovaHealth reported a sustained wave of 502/503 responses and streaming disconnects starting 2026-03-12 09:10 UTC. Support observed amplified traffic from the NovaHealth client SDK that correlated with repeated request retries. Impact: customer-facing outages for NovaHealth production traffic (~120 rps baseline, observed 9x during peak), degraded latency platform-wide in affected region, increased 5xx rate and elevated costs. Environment: Production (us-east-1), customer uses Redwood Private (VPC) with SDK v1.3.4 embedded in their app. Observed behavior: API Gateway returned 502/503s under load; upstream serving-runtime reported connection churn and elevated active connections. Expected behavior: client respects Retry-After/X-RateLimit headers and backs off gracefully, avoiding amplified load and 5xx waves.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Deploy client app using Redwood SDK v1.3.4 with default retry middleware and tenant API key.
2) Send steady-state traffic (~120 rps) to a pinned model endpoint (redwood-v2-large).
3) Inject a simulated transient upstream slowdown (e.g., delay model init or reduce concurrency) to trigger a 5xx response for a subset of requests.
4) Observe SDK retry behavior and API Gateway metrics; note any immediate retry spikes following 5xx/429 responses.
logs: [2026-03-12T09:11:03Z] sdk::retry WARN compute_backoff: parsed X-RateLimit-Reset=1610000000000 (treated as ms), computed_delay=-1200ms -> clamped to 0ms
[2026-03-12T09:11:04Z] serving-runtime ERROR connection_watchdog: rapid reconnects from 10.2.1.45 (tenant novahealth) -> restart triggered
comments: Support (2026-03-12T09:20Z) - Maya Chen: Initial triage completed. Correlation between repeated immediate retries from NovaHealth SDK instances and apigw 5xx spike. Gathering logs and SDK version info.
Customer (2026-03-12T09:28Z) - NovaHealth SRE (Priya Rao): Confirmed SDK v1.3.4, observed app-level error bursts and higher CPU usage. Can provide timeline and deployment manifest on request.

Eng (2026-03-12T10:05Z) - Luis Ortega: Reproduced locally. SDK v1.3.4 parses X-RateLimit-Reset header as milliseconds instead of epoch seconds when header value length > 12; leads to negative backoff and immediate retry. Filing internal fix and staging patch.

Support (2026-03-12T11:30Z) - Maya Chen: Applied customer-side mitigation: advised NovaHealth to pin SDK to 1.3.2 or toggle retry middleware off. Customer applied temporary rollback and reported immediate drop in retry amplification.
investigation_notes: Hypothesis: malformed/large X-RateLimit-Reset value gets misinterpreted by SDK parser; edge-case numeric parsing bug introduced in v1.3.4.
Checked apigw logs and observed retry loop timestamps aligned with negative/zero computed backoff in SDK logs.
Serving-runtime showed repeated short-lived connections and repeated model loading attempts for some worker processes, increasing memory pressure and triggering watchdog restarts.
Customer traffic volume combined with immediate retries amplified load beyond autoscaler warm-up window causing transient 5xx saturation in the region.
No evidence of intentional DDoS. Issue is deterministic with SDK v1.3.4 when X-RateLimit-Reset is large (e.g., clients receiving reset epoch seconds > 1e12).
resolution: Mitigation steps: 1) Instructed NovaHealth to roll back to SDK v1.3.2 (done) — immediate improvement confirmed. 2) Deployed a server-side defensive clamp in API Gateway to convert suspicious reset values to sane defaults and return 429 + Retry-After when appropriate (rolled to canary at 2026-03-12T14:00Z). 3) Engineering released SDK patch v1.3.5 that fixes X-RateLimit-Reset parsing and adds defensive clamping for negative delays; patch scheduled for customer upgrade on 2026-03-13. 4) Temporarily increased tenant capacity for NovaHealth for 4 hours to avoid customer impact while patch rolled out. Postmortem and action items assigned.
